jurisdiction.name: Fiji
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Fiji has no AI-specific law or framework yet. AI is steered by two plans: the National Digital Strategy 2025-2030, endorsed by Cabinet in April 2025, which promises a National AI Framework that has not yet been published, and the National Development Plan 2025-2029, which calls for an AI roadmap and a regulatory sandbox. The Investment Act 2021 requires ministerial approval for foreign investment in critical technologies such as AI. Data protection exists only as a policy endorsed by Cabinet in October 2025; there is no data protection law.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Trade, Co-operatives, MSME and Communications
narrative.review_notes: This review was carried out on 13 October 2026 from the official laws portal, Parliament's bills list and government websites. Not yet verified from the official text: any AI material from the main digital government site, the Online Safety Commission and the education ministry. The promised National AI Framework and the data protection policy, whose text is not online, are tracked as leads.

instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Trade, Co-operatives, Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises and Communications (Digital Government Transformation Office), Government of the Republic of Fiji
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Trade, Co-operatives, Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises and Communications
instruments.summary: Fiji's first national digital strategy, a five-year roadmap built on five pillars (infrastructure and cyber resilience, skilled workforce, digital inclusion, innovation-led growth and smart governance). Under smart governance it commits to a National AI Framework that will ensure ethical AI adoption by addressing data privacy, accountability and governance and promote responsible AI integration in government and private-sector services, plus an AI-driven government services chatbot piloted in selected ministries. It also commits to specific legal provisions for emerging technologies such as AI with a regulatory sandbox, lists 'Develop a National AI Framework' among 2025 milestones and an AI policy and framework for healthcare, and sets up a National Digital Economy Committee, a National Digital Sub-committee and an Implementation Unit to oversee delivery.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Main national policy anchoring AI governance in Fiji; commits the Government to a National AI Framework (not yet published as of 2026-10-13).
instruments.current_status: Endorsed by Cabinet at its 5th meeting on 1 April 2025 (official Cabinet decisions release) and launched in April 2025 (Minister Vosarogo's Fiji Tech Summit 2025 address on fiji.gov.fj: 'In April, we launched Fiji's first-ever National Digital Strategy 2025-2030'); the document itself states only '(c) 2025'. In force for 2025-2030. The National AI Framework it promises had not been published as of 2026-10-13 (see leads). A copy is also hosted by the Telecommunications Authority of Fiji (taf.org.fj).

instruments.official_title: Fiji National Development Plan 2025-2029 and Vision 2050
instruments.english_title: Fiji National Development Plan 2025-2029 and Vision 2050
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Finance, Strategic Planning, National Development and Statistics, Government of the Republic of Fiji
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Finance, Strategic Planning, National Development and Statistics
instruments.summary: Fiji's five-year national development plan and long-term Vision 2050, organised around economic resilience, people empowerment and good governance. Its research, development and innovation chapter gives special focus to Industrial Revolution 4.0 technologies, in particular AI, with strategies to adopt AI across economic sectors and public-sector delivery, develop a national RDI roadmap for IR4.0 and AI including an institutional governance framework, and introduce a promotive regulatory framework with a regulatory sandbox. It sets a key performance indicator of a 'Roadmap for IR4.0 Technology - AI' completed within 3 years and implemented within 5 years.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Top-level national plan that commits the Government to an AI roadmap with an institutional governance framework; AI is a named priority rather than the plan's main subject.
instruments.current_status: Launched on 17 September 2024 (Deputy Prime Minister Kamikamica's launch speech on fiji.gov.fj, dated Sep 17, 2024); the document states '(c) 2024'. Covers 2025-2029. The AI roadmap it calls for had not been published as of 2026-10-13.

instruments.issuing_authority: Parliament of the Republic of Fiji
instruments.publisher_name: Parliament of the Republic of Fiji
instruments.summary: Fiji's general foreign and domestic investment law. Section 7 lets the Minister prohibit a foreign direct investment to protect national security and requires a foreign investor intending to invest in a sector that may affect critical technologies 'such as artificial intelligence, robotics, semiconductors' (among other listed sectors) to submit the investment proposal to the Minister for approval; the approval process may be prescribed by regulations.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: General law with an explicit AI provision: foreign investment in AI is subject to national-security approval under s 7(2)(b).
instruments.current_status: Act No. 5 of 2021, passed by Parliament on 3 June 2021 (date printed beneath the assent: [3 June 2021]). In force from 1 August 2022 under Legal Notice No. 72 of 2022 (Investment Act 2021 Commencement Notice, dated 10 May 2022, Government of Fiji Gazette Supplement No. 21 of 11 May 2022), made under s 1(2). The Laws of Fiji portal serves the as-published Act through its API (base64 PDF in JSON); the consolidated text (Cap 221A) is on the same portal.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: The Laws of Fiji portal, Parliament's bills list, the government, ministries and regulators were searched at national level. No qualifying AI-governance document was found for risk and assurance, procurement, cybersecurity, data protection, transparency, standards, readiness indices, sector rules, generative AI, drafts and consultations, international agreements, or past instruments. Material of the main digital government site and the Online Safety Commission, education ministry and trade ministry, the official text of the national privacy and personal data protection policy and the National AI Framework (a lead) remain to be checked.
coverage_audit.technical_note:
Coverage note (original): Technical review notes: tier B/C batch run 2026-10-13, one agent, national level only (PROTOCOL §6), about 25-minute time box. digital.gov.fj proxy 502 (mobile.digital.gov.fj works); osc.gov.fj, mtcsme.gov.fj proxy 502; education.gov.fj reset. laws.gov.fj searched (AI, deepfake, automated decision, algorithm) and laws-as-published index 2017-2026; source_url is the portal API endpoint (SPA deep links 404 to curl). Strategy dated 2025-04 from official launch speech (document '© 2025'); Cabinet endorsement 2025-04-01 per Cabinet decisions release. Investment Act kept: s 7(2)(b) AI-specific approval duty; publication 2021-06-03 (date beneath assent), in force 2022-08-01 (LN 72 of 2022). Convention 108: not a party (Cabinet release 7 Oct 2025 says Fiji will take steps to join 108+). Units covered: Law: Laws of Fiji portal (laws.gov.fj) own search for 'artificial intelligence', 'deepfake', 'automated decision', 'algorithm' plus the laws-as-published index: only AI provision is Investment Act 2021 s 7(2)(b) (recorded). No AI law, no data protection Act, no deepfake offence. Parliament bills list 2018-2026: no AI or data protection bill. Online Safety Act 2018 and Cybercrime Act 2021 contain no AI provisions.; Government: National Digital Strategy 2025-2030 (recorded), National Development Plan 2025-2029 (recorded); fiji.gov.fj search and Cabinet releases checked. No national AI strategy, AI framework, public-sector AI/GenAI guideline or procurement guidance published (National AI Framework is a lead).; Ministries: Searched, nothing found: Education (AI integration discussed publicly, no policy document; education.gov.fj unreachable), Health (AI policy only as an NDS outcome), Finance, Justice, Defence/Policing, Labour, Agriculture (E-Agriculture Strategy 2026-2031 is a lead).; Regulators: Searched, nothing found: Reserve Bank of Fiji (site search: no AI guidance), Fijian Competition and Consumer Commission (site search: none), Telecommunications Authority of Fiji (none), Online Safety Commission (site unreachable; no official AI guidance found), no data protection authority exists, no national cyber agency AI guidance (Fiji CERT).. Not reached: digital.gov.fj main site (502 via proxy; only mobile.digital.gov.fj reachable); osc.gov.fj (502); education.gov.fj (connection reset); mtcsme.gov.fj (502). Could not verify: Official text of the National Privacy and Personal Data Protection Policy (endorsed 7 Oct 2025); Online Safety Commission AI material (site unreachable); Ministry of Education AI material (site unreachable). risk-assurance, procurement, cyber-security, data-privacy, transparency, standards, index-readiness, sectoral, generative-ai, drafts, international, historical: no material found.
